articles.headline: Seven things Solak thinks entering NFL Week 4
articles.description: Bowers will go off under Klint Kubiak? The Rams need another pass catcher? Steelers-Browns will be fun? And Lamar Jackson for MVP? Get ready for Week 4 with some takes.
articles.body:
Who's ready to put their thinking caps on? Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season will go down in the history books, as 12 -- count 'em, 12! -- Sunday games finished within one score, the new single-day record for the league. Toss in two fun primetime games on Thursday and Monday and that was about as good a week as NFL football gets.

Every Tuesday of the NFL season, I'll turn the page from the previous week to the upcoming one with seven things I think. These aren't full-scale predictions; those come later. They aren't concrete takeaways from the past week of NFL action, either; those are fired off Sunday or Monday. Instead, these are the uncertain topics. They are things that might be true, but it'll probably take the next few games to find out. And at the bottom, you'll find a few extra half-thoughts ... just those little inklings I'm unable to shake.

This week, I'll start with the one player I've been most excited to see in his new system, make another pick for MVP (I'm up to two in three weeks) and highlight an intradivisional game between surprising 2-1 teams you should probably watch for fun. Here are seven things I think ahead of Week 4.

Jump to:

Bowers is the new JSN

Jackson for league MVP

Lawrence reminds us to be patient with QBs

Rams should make one more trade

Steelers-Browns is suddenly important

I will never trust the Bills

McCarthy won't save the Giants

Five extra inklings

I think ... Brock Bowers is the new Jaxon Smith-Njigba

We had to wait a few extra weeks for it, but one of the most anticipated debuts of the 2026 season struck Sunday. Bowers, the third-year Raiders tight end fresh off a meniscus cleanup, took his first snaps in Klint Kubiak's offense against the Saints. The final card? Ten catches, 116 yards and a score. Bowers has four career games of 10-plus receptions, 100-plus yards and a touchdown. Since he entered the league in 2024, the rest of the NFL's tight ends combined have only four such games.

So, he picked up where he left off.

Watching Bowers is such a delight. He has receiver-like instincts and catch technique. He has receiver-like movement skills. He can run receiver-esque routes -- routes other coaches wouldn't think to ask of their tight ends.

Now, you've likely heard other tight ends erroneously called "quasi-wide receivers." Analysts were obsessed with flex tight ends in the prime of Travis Kelce and Mark Andrews, so we started throwing the label around willy-nilly. It's important, in our appreciation of what Bowers brings to the Raiders' offense, to be objective about the uniqueness of his impact.

Think of a smaller pass-catching tight end who's having a productive year: Dalton Kincaid with the Bills has been a breakout star. Against the Lions in Week 2, Kincaid had seven targets from traditional wide receiver alignments -- either in the slot or wide -- which was one of the highest among all tight ends this season. articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Liverpool keen on Real Madrid midfielder Tchouaméni
articles.description: Liverpool have maintained contact with the representatives of Real Madrid midfielder Aurélien Tchouaméni. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.body:
Real Madrid midfielder Aurélien Tchouaméni is still on the radar of Liverpool, while Internazionale are eyeing a January move for USMNT and Crystal Palace defender Chris Richards. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Liverpool have maintained contact with the representatives of Real Madrid midfielder Aurélien Tchouaméni despite the 26-year-old signing a new deal until 2031, according to TEAMtalk. While the Reds are not actively pursuing the France international right now, they could revive their interest if his role under José Mourinho changes given he has only played three times so far this season. Madrid had reportedly been willing to listen to offers of around €80 million over the summer.

- Internazionale are eyeing a January move for USMNT and Crystal Palace defender Chris Richards, according to Tuttosport. Inter scouts have been tracking the 26-year-old, who operates on the right side of Palace's back three, as part of the club's plan to bring in free agents. Richards' contract expires in 2027 and he could bolster a defense already containing new arrivals Djed Spence and John Stones.

- Manchester City will refuse to allow striker Erling Haaland to leave on the cheap even if they face relegation as a result of their legal battle with the Premier League, reports Football Insider. Arsenal, Real Madrid and Barcelona are paying close attention to the 26-year-old's situation, but City hold a strong negotiating position as his contract runs until 2034 with no relegation release clause.

- Chelsea remain interested in signing Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara in January despite his €55 million deadline-day transfer collapsing, according to TEAMtalk. Liverpool, Crystal Palace, Brighton & Hove Albion and Newcastle United are also tracking the 22-year-old Senegal international, who is keen on a January switch, though Monaco's willingness to sanction his exit remains uncertain.

- Beşiktaş president Serdal Adalı has vowed to sign Newcastle United midfielder Joe Willock in January, as per TalkSPORT. The 27-year-old is in the final year of his contract and can agree to a pre-contract with overseas clubs in January, though he has featured regularly under new boss Matthias Jaissle this season.

Other rumors

- Paris Saint-Germain, Manchester United and Arsenal are tracking FC Porto right-back Alberto Costa, 22. (Caught Offside)

- Manchester United and Liverpool are scouting 16-year-old Gambian winger Alieu Saine at the WAFU Zone A Under-17 tournament, alongside Benfica and Celta Vigo. (Football Insider)

- Liverpool, Real Madrid, and Barcelona are all keeping tabs on Borussia Dortmund defender Nico Schlotterbeck. (Ekrem Konur)

- Bayern Munich will face major hurdles if they attempt to sign Everton goalkeeper Jordan Pickford, who remains under contract until 2029. (TEAMtalk)

- AC Milan are preparing to intensify their pursuit of Barcelona left

articles.headline: 2026 NFL Power Rankings: How all 32 teams stack up for Week 4
articles.description: How do all 32 NFL teams stack up through three weeks? Plus, we picked out each team's biggest fantasy surprise -- good or bad.
articles.body:
Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season was filled with close matchups. There were 12 games decided by eight or fewer points Sunday, tying the record for the most such matchups in a single day, per ESPN Research.

Along with those close contests came plenty of intriguing fantasy performances. So in addition to our 1-32 rankings, we asked our NFL Nation reporters to look at every team's fantasy football surprise (good or bad) this season. They went off ESPN Fantasy's draft rankings, average draft position (ADP) and current scoring leaders in PPR leagues.

To form the list, our power panel of more than a dozen NFL analysts evaluates how all 32 teams stack up against one another, ranking them from No. 1 to 32. And here are a few highlights from this week's rankings:

The 3-0 Raiders are shooting up our list, climbing six spots after doing the same last week. They're the first team in the common draft era (since 1967) to start 3-0 after selecting a QB No. 1 (Fernando Mendoza) in the previous draft, per ESPN Research. And against the Saints, they broke a franchise-worst streak of 39 regular-season games in which they failed to score 30 points.

New England fell six more spots after quarterback Drake Maye registered a 15.5 Total QBR in a blowout loss to the Jaguars -- a career worst with at least 15 dropbacks. Through three games, the Patriots' offense is averaging the lowest EPA per play and points per drive by any team since the 2023 Jets, who had Zach Wilson at QB, per ESPN Research.

After starting 0-3, the Buccaneers are ahead of only the Titans and Dolphins. This is the team's worst record to begin a season since 2014, when it finished 2-14 in its first year under current general manager Jason Licht. And things might not get easier for the Bucs, who are expected to play undrafted rookie free agent Jalon Daniels in place of the injured Baker Mayfield (thumb) for at least the next three weeks.

Let's get into the full list, starting with the same No. 1 team as last week.

articles.headline: Man City learned of guilty verdicts in summer before transfer activity - sources
articles.description: Manchester City were first informed that they had been found guilty of more than 100 breaches of the Premier League's financial rules in the summer, sources told ESPN, before spending heavily in the transfer market.
articles.body:
Manchester City were first informed that they had been found guilty of more than 100 breaches of the Premier League's financial rules in the summer, sources told ESPN, before spending heavily in the transfer market.

News of a verdict in the case against was made public Friday. But sources told ESPN that club chiefs were initially made aware of the findings of the independent panel in July. It was followed by an aggressive approach in the summer transfer window during which seven senior signings arrived at the Etihad Stadium at a cost of more than £450 million ($596m).

City twice broke their own transfer record to sign Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest for £116m and Enzo Fernández from Chelsea for a joint-British record £125m.

According to sources, the deal for Anderson was agreed before City had knowledge that the independent panel had reached its verdict. A deal for his signing was agreed on July 2 before he officially signed on July 23.

City declined to comment when approached by ESPN on Tuesday. The Premier League said Friday that it would not comment on a "private and confidential process."

City's summer transfer business has helped Enzo Maresca's team make a flying start to the new season with seven wins from seven in all competitions.

They sit top of the Premier League table -- three points clear of defending champions Arsenal -- after winning each of their first five games.

- Wayne Rooney wouldn't 'feel comfortable' accepting Premier League medal if Man City stripped of titles

- Man City CEO adamant legal battle with the Premier League is not over - reports

- Man City vs. Premier League: 115 financial charges explained

City have maintained their innocence since Premier League charges were first announced in February 2023. Club sources have made it clear they intend to appeal any guilty verdict.

A statement issued Friday read: "The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality.

"As such Manchester City FC's position remains consistent with the club's statement of February 2023.

"The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence."

articles.headline: Fantasy football buzz: Case Keenum to the rescue as Bears dominate Eagles on Monday Night Football
articles.description: Case Keenum came up big on Monday Night Football, elevating the Bears offense accounting for three touchdowns.
articles.body:
Everything that happens in the NFL has additional context when viewed from a fantasy football perspective. From position battles to injuries and so much more, the news cycle will constantly affect player values in fantasy football.

Our fantasy football buzz file, with contributions from our ESPN fantasy writers and our NFL Nation reporters, aims to provide fantasy managers with the intel they need as news breaks around the league.

Sept. 29: Case Keenum to the Monday Night rescue

By Michael F. Florio

Case Keenum was the star of the show on Monday Night Football, emerging from third on the Bears QB depth chart in Week 2 to make the Week 3 start, his first since Dec. 24, 2023. He threw for 247 yards and two touchdowns, completing 71% of his passes. He also added six rushing yards and a touchdown. He finished with 24.48 fantasy points, meaning he has more in one game than Drake Maye does on the season (21.6).

Keenum could be in line to start again in Week 4, and would be in play in superflex leagues against a Jets secondary that has been tough to pass on this season. Tyson Bagent would be the other Bears option while Caleb Williams recovers from his hamstring injury.

Kalif Raymond led the Bears in receiving yards for the second time in three weeks. He and Luther Burden III have been the Bears' top two target-getters in each game. Through three weeks, He is second on the team in targets. He should be the top WR waiver wire pickup, as he is available in almost 90% of leagues. Burden had a big night of his own, seeing a team-high 11 targets, turning them into seven catches for 61 yards and a touchdown. He also added in a 7-yard run. He leads the Bears in targets and has a 32% red zone target share. Burden is blossoming into the must-start option fantasy managers envisioned during draft season.

Both Colston Loveland and Rome Odunze just missed touchdowns. Loveland dove and was down just short of the goal line at the one. Meanwhile, Odunze had an open touchdown slip through his hands. In total, Odunze turned six targets into three catches for 44 yards. Loveland finished with four catches for 31 yards on four targets. Both players' fantasy stocks remain down. Loveland is in play just because the lack of high-ceiling options at tight end. Odunze though is purely a flex option that should hit a good amount of benches until we see otherwise.

The Bears did not duplicate the rushing success that they had in 2025, but D'Andre Swift did have himself a nice showing. He played 70% of the snaps with 20 carries for 84 yards. He also caught two of three targets for four yards. While he did not score a touchdown, he was used often in the red zone. Kyle Monangai finished with 10 carries for 31 yards. He is a top insurance back but has had trouble finding standalone value.

Bronny on LeBron James' Lakers exit: 'He's got his own path'

Sept. 28

Bronny on LeBron James' Lakers exit: 'He's got his own path'

When LeBron James chose to leave the Los Angeles Lakers in free agency over the summer, he consulted his family on the decision to sign with the Philadelphia 76ers. But when it came to his son/teammate Bronny, much was apparently left unsaid.

"We're men of very little words when it comes to talking about business and what we're going to do and how we feel about each other. So it wasn't really much [discussion] to be honest with you," Bronny James said Monday at Lakers media day.

"He's got his own path and I got my own. He knows that I want to make a name for myself and I want to continue my career and keep growing as a player. And he knows that I want to focus on that. So he decided to do that."

LeBron and Bronny have routinely been in unique situations in league history, whether it was opening night two years ago, when the father and son entered the game together, or last year in the playoffs, where they combined to deliver a 10-0 run during a victory over the Houston Rockets. Navigating a complex free agency in which the father leaves and the son stays is another one for the books.

 Tatum 'comfortable' leading new-look Celtics post-Brown trade

Jayson Tatum's one constant during his development into a star with the Boston Celtics was having Jaylen Brown as a teammate.

That partnership ended this offseason when the Celtics' front office decided to trade Brown -- the 2024 NBA Finals MVP -- to the Philadelphia 76ers in what was largely a cost-cutting move that broke up the duo most responsible for leading Boston to the 2024 NBA championship.

articles.headline: Fantasy basketball: Eric Karabell's 'Do Draft' list
articles.description: Eric Karabell highlights the players who are falling further than they should be in fantasy basketball drafts this season.
articles.body:
When the much-maligned Julius Randle was the best player for the New York Knicks, before, you know, they eagerly jettisoned him toward the Minnesota Timberwolves in the Karl-Anthony Towns trade and won an NBA championship, he was one of the more underrated fantasy options around. I would marvel at how Randle consistently would be available outside the top 50 of drafts, despite numbers that clearly warranted better. After all, in our game, the numbers are what matters.

Remember, starting with the 2020-21 season, when Randle earned the league's Most Improved Player award, he averaged 23.2 PPG, 10.0 RPG and 5.1 APG for three Knicks seasons. He was durable, appearing in 71 or more games each season, and he led the league with 37.6 MPG that first year. No, we didn't always enjoy the shooting and turnovers, but this wasn't a top 25 option in drafts, either. Randle earned two All-Star selections, and from a fantasy aspect, routinely outperformed his ADP in fantasy drafts.

Get ready for more of that version of Randle, because the Timberwolves dumped his contract on the Brooklyn Nets this offseason, and the big numbers are coming back. They must! The Nets, if you haven't noticed, are not exactly loaded. Randle and Michael Porter Jr. will get all the usage they desire. They will score the points and, assuming they feel like it, garner myriad rebounds, too. Randle should feel like it. His usage will skyrocket. The Nets may not win much, but fantasy managers don't care. Randle, 31, should deliver the solid statistics we recall from his Knicks days and, looking at early ADP, few seem terribly interested.

Randle's efforts haven't always helped his NBA teams to much success -- the Knicks won a single playoff series in his five seasons, he played a lesser role for last season's Timberwolves, and he missed the playoffs with the Los Angeles Lakers and New Orleans Pelicans -- but the numbers helped us, the greedy fantasy managers. Randle is a top 50 fantasy option, but sans that level of draft day commitment. Go get him.

Welcome to the latest "Do Draft" list for fantasy basketball. I do this every season, highlighting players I feel warrant earlier attention as related to their general ADP. We know ADP varies by site, but we can tell who potential managers target and those they do not. Consider durability, age, role and other factors, of course, but sometimes the risk is worth the reward. In addition to Randle, here are others that should be getting picked earlier in drafts.

James Harden, PG/SG, Cleveland Cavaliers: We are seeing a larger range of ADP possibilities than typical for Harden but, even if goes early in Round 2, he is worth it! Harden, 37, has never really failed to produce numbers. Worried about durability? He played in more than 70 games each of the past three seasons. He scores, passes, hits free throws and plays.
